title: The Box
context: Nora just found a ring box in her boyfriend's drawer.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: I was just looking for a phone charger.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: That's a ring box. That is absolutely a ring box.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Three years together, and he's finally going to ask me.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Okay. Breathe. Don't open it. Let him have his moment.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: Babe, I'm home! I got your favorite dumplings!

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Act normal. Smile. Be a person who found nothing.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Because I think I know what's coming.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: I know. I know. Don't tell her yet.

shots.keyframe: Extreme close-up over Nora's shoulder: a round oak nightstand drawer pulled open, a small dark green velvet ring box glowing under a warm bedside lamp, Nora's fingertips (mustard cardigan sleeve) frozen an inch above it, a phone charger cable in her other hand. Honey light.
shots.motion: Slow push-in on the box; her fingers tremble slightly; the lamp glow pulses once.

shots.keyframe: Close-up of Nora's face, eyes wide and shining, hand over her mouth, warm lamp light on her cheek, small yellow hair clip in her hair.
shots.motion: She gasps; her eyes flick down to the box and back; a tiny joyful bounce of her shoulders; slow dolly-in.

shots.keyframe: Dreamy imagined scene: a rooftop at golden hour with string lights, Sam kneeling as a soft-focus silhouette holding up a small ring box, warm glowing dreamy haze and vignette.
shots.motion: Gentle crane up; dust motes drift like confetti; the frame softly breathes.

shots.keyframe: Medium shot of Nora closing the nightstand drawer slowly with two fingers, biting her lip to hold back a grin, amber bedroom with sage-green walls.
shots.motion: The drawer slides shut slowly; she pats it twice and tiptoes backward; the camera tracks with her.

shots.keyframe: Wide shot down the cozy apartment hallway toward the front door: Sam (green flannel, round glasses, curly black hair) shouldering through the door with a paper takeout bag, warm lamps; Nora in the near foreground, back to camera, mid-flinch.
shots.motion: Sam pushes the door shut with his foot and lifts the bag; Nora jumps and spins away, smoothing her cardigan.

shots.keyframe: Medium shot of Nora sitting at a small kitchen table, hands folded like a student, an exaggerated calm smile, eyes darting sideways; sage-green cabinets behind her, a tomato plant on the fire-escape window.
shots.motion: She straightens her cardigan and blinks too many times; tiny camera drift.

shots.keyframe: Over-the-shoulder from Sam's side of the table (his hand with a worn leather watch setting down a dumpling takeout box), Nora across the table in candlelight, glowing, hopeful eyes.
shots.motion: Sam's hand slides the box toward her; Nora's smile widens and wobbles with nerves; slow push-in on her eyes; steam rises from the dumplings.

shots.keyframe: Nora's point of view through a half-open bedroom door: Sam's back, shoulders tense, phone at his ear, lit by a cold teal window at the end of the hallway; the warm kitchen glow at the foreground edge.
shots.motion: Slow creeping push toward the gap in the door; Sam rubs the back of his neck and turns further away; the light shifts from amber to teal.

shots.keyframe: Close-up of Nora's face at the door gap, the warmth gone from her cheeks, her smile fading into confusion, cool teal side light.
shots.motion: Her smile slowly falls; her eyes lift toward the camera; a quick small push-in, then stillness.

cliffhanger: Through the door Nora hears Sam on the phone say "Don't tell her yet."

posting.caption: She wasn't snooping. She just needed a charger. Then she heard that phone call. Would you have asked him right away, or waited? Part 2 tomorrow. #lovestory #animatedstory #storytime #relationshipdrama #ringinthedrawer
